page.layout: Top: page number and running head across the top of the page. Below them, one column of running text, full width. Under the text, a rule, then a centred chapter heading with a title, a thesis label, and a paragraph beginning with a woodcut initial. A catchword sits at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: non determinetur a causis secundis, quoad specificationem actionis, siquidem determinandi vox sumatur proprie, iisdem rationibus colligi potest. Nam quod objicias, in conferendo concursu Deum sequi naturam & conditionem causarum secun-darum, talemque semper concursum praebere, qualem illae exigunt, nihil est. Hinc enim non sequitur, concursum Dei a causis secundis determinari, sed hoc tantum se-quitur, naturam & modum operandi in causis secundis esse rationem objectivam, quae talem concursum requirat, qualem Deus tribuit, sed pro arbitratu suo, sive quia ita decrevit. Nam quemadmodum Deus ab aeterno certas res decrevit, certo tempo-re producere certa naturae conditione & agendi potestate praeditas; ita quoque decrevit ab aeterno cum iisdem rebus ad operandum sic concurrere, ut natura singula-rum postulat.
main_text.head: CAP. XII. De Substantia Creata.
main_text.p: Actum est de Deo, sequitur Creatu-ra; qua voce intelligimus substan-tiam a Deo factam ex nihilo. Nam

page.notes: Dark smudge at the top right corner and a short dash at the bottom centre are marks on the scan, not print, so they are left out. The ornamental rule above the chapter heading is a printer's rule and is not transcribed as text. "THESIS I." is set in spaced capitals; I followed the rule for numbered theses and wrote it as a paragraph, not a heading. The initial "A" is a woodcut letter joined to "ctum" as "Actum". The catchword "accidentia" is set at the right with a stroke before it.
